scene.metaphor: A radiologist’s signal hunt rendered as a miniature light-table world: one clean chest-film shape discovered inside a stack of translucent noisy sheets.
scene.setting: Polished studio tabletop set on a cool-gray surface, with a low lateral miniature lightbox stretching across the frame and lots of open negative space above and around it.
scene.frozen_incident: Tal leans in with a focused, slightly amused expression as a tiny fan has just nudged several translucent film layers askew, exposing one crisp mint-tinted silhouette beneath the noise.
physical_materials: stacked translucent acetate film sheets with cloudy gray speckle
miniature cobalt clip and mint marker tab
subtle coral accent in Tal’s tank top
scene.image_instruction: Create a polished editorial studio photograph in a cool-gray palette with cobalt and mint accents and only one restrained warm note. Tal Perry must be clearly recognizable: curly dark hair, salt-and-pepper beard, expressive eyes, and a grounded, observant presence. Place him as an operator-observer at a low, horizontal miniature light-table set so the composition reads across a 3:1 banner and still holds as a single dominant silhouette at thumbnail size. In front of him, stack three to five translucent acetate chest-film sheets over a frosted acrylic lightbox; each sheet carries soft cloudy noise, speckle, and faint layered shadows. At the frozen instant, a tiny fan has just slid the top sheets sideways, revealing one crisp mint-lit chest silhouette beneath the clutter. Tal pinches one corner with tweezers or a gloved fingertip, leaning in with a calm, satisfied half-smile as if he has found the one reliable signal. Keep props to a maximum of three large supporting forms, with generous negative space, high tonal separation, and serious studio lighting that makes the absurd miniature world feel tactile and precise.
